% recipe its numbered section with a serving line, its ingredients and its numbered steps.
\documentclass[preset=cookbook]{ltflow}
\begin{document}
\chapter{Breads}
\begin{recipe}{Flat bread}{Serves four; thirty minutes}
\begin{itemize}
\item two cups of flour;
\item one cup of water;
\item a pinch of salt.
\end{itemize}
\begin{enumerate}
\item Mix the flour, water and salt into a soft dough and rest it for ten minutes.
\item Divide it into four, roll each piece thin and cook it on a hot dry pan until it puffs.
\end{enumerate}
\end{recipe}
\begin{recipe}{Seeded rolls}{Makes eight; two hours}
\begin{itemize}
\item three cups of flour;
\item a spoon of seeds;
\item one cup of warm water.
\end{itemize}
\begin{enumerate}
\item Knead everything for ten minutes and leave the dough to rise for an hour.
\item Shape eight rolls, scatter the seeds over them and bake until they sound hollow.
\end{enumerate}
\end{recipe}
\chapter{Soups}
\begin{recipe}{Green soup}{Serves two; twenty minutes}
\begin{itemize}
\item a bunch of greens;
\item one onion;
\item two cups of stock.
\end{itemize}
\begin{enumerate}
\item Soften the onion, add the stock and the greens and simmer for ten minutes.
\item Blend until smooth and season to taste.
\end{enumerate}
\end{recipe}
\end{document}
